newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end lower on stronger yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end lower on stronger yen.

text.p: All months of Tokyo corn futures closed lower on Thursday, as the yen's gains against the dollar triggered active selling by local investors, traders said.
Prices were 80 to 110 yen lower, with the benchmark November 1997 down 110 yen at 14,030 yen per tonne. Daily volume was 33,634 lots.
The yen's advances against the dollar, triggered by comments from a senior Ministry of Finance official, produced active selling from local investors, the traders said.
"But we were encouraged by the fact the benchmark November contract was supported above 14,000 yen," one trader said.
The spot December contract on the CBOT Project A corn trading system was being traded at $2.60-1/4 per bushel at 0900 GMT, against $2.60 at Wednesday's close.
The spot November of the CBOT soybean futures on the Project A overnight trading system was at $6.81 at 0900 GMT, against $6.81 at Wednesday's close.
